foundation.appearance: Match the measured footage: natural look, standard contrast, Rec.709, mostly tripod or smooth gimbal, sharp. Outdoor daylight on sandy ground under trees, warm sun with soft shade, true-to-life colour: red-orange burnt clay bricks, grey wet cement mortar, beige and white cotton shirts, dark trousers, green foliage. Muted, not saturated; no grading look, no filters, no haze added. AI scenes are photographic and documentary, eye-level or slightly high, never glossy or advertising.

editing_constraints.statement: Two footage shots were rejected at the first cut: C0089 (masons clearing the work surface) under 'Construction begins…' and C0100 (joint finishing) under 'pointing is carried out'; neither returns in those slots.

exclusions.source: direction: nothing staged as the client's own site or result
exclusions.statement: No AI scene shows the client's signboards (Takshashila, Nachiketa), the VK NARDEP campus or its people; AI scenes are representative places.
No figure appears that the script does not say: only 25 percent and 20, 35 and 75 kg/cm²; the comparable-strength graphic carries no numbers.

exclusions.source: script: good practice is the message
exclusions.statement: No shot shows mortar dropped into the cavities, bricks laid flat in a rat-trap wall, or a dry, uncured wall presented as finished.

graphic_style.background: Flat warm cream, no texture or gradient.
graphic_style.frame_fill: The drawing fills about 70% of the frame, centred, with a calm margin for labels.
graphic_style.labels: Short sentence-case phrases in a plain sans serif, charcoal on cream, at least 4% of frame height (titles 6%), leader lines ending on their part.
graphic_style.line_weight: Clean 3 px charcoal outlines at 1080p, 1.5 px for brick joints; no hatching.
graphic_style.palette: Terracotta red-orange for brick (#B5562F), warm cream background (#F3E9DA), charcoal lines and text (#2B2B2B), mortar grey (#9A9A94), air and cavity a pale sky blue (#BFD8E6), heat a warm amber (#E39B2D), one accent green for 'saved' (#5E8C4A).

production_constraints.statement: The approved first cut, its narration and timing are fixed; pictures fill the gaps only.

specifications.statement: 16:9, 1920x1080, 25 fps, watched with sound on website and YouTube.
Figures exactly as narrated: nearly 25% fewer bricks; minimum crushing strength 20 kg/cm² (single-storey), 35 kg/cm² (two-storey), 75 kg/cm² (three-storey); at least seven days of curing.

foundation.treatment: By the end the viewer should understand that the hollow cavities are the point of rat-trap bond (fewer bricks and less mortar, a cooler home, strength enough for up to three storeys) and should have seen the careful work it needs. This is a documentary explainer told from the site: the real footage of masons at work carries the film, and the gaps are filled two ways. Where a camera could have filmed it with more time (housing construction, the plinth, guide strings, kilns, pointing, curing, finished homes and the people in them), a realistic representative AI scene, muted and true to life to match the footage (natural daylight, a red-brick site in Tamil Nadu, nothing staged as the client's own site or result). Where the meaning is invisible to a camera (the cavity inside the wall, heat, load, the brick saving, strength by storey, the sill course), one drawn cutaway of a rat-trap bond wall that comes back and develops across the film, in one graphic language, with the script's own figures drawn exactly.

world.scope: every rat-trap wall, drawn or scene
world.source: clip findings across C0091, C0104, C0115, C0116; script
world.statement: Rat-trap bond: bricks laid on edge, two outer faces with headers across, leaving continuous rectangular cavities inside the wall, joints in grey cement-sand mortar.
Tools are the site's own: pointed steel trowel with a wooden handle, a shallow round iron mortar pan (tasla), wooden or aluminium straightedge, plumb bob on a wooden block, coconut-midrib broom.

scene.light: Mid-morning sun high to one side of the street, warm white and strong: hard sunlight on the brick walls and sand, soft shade under the neem trees; true-to-life colour matching the footage's natural daylight.
scene.air: clean, a little dust lifting near the brick stack

landmarks.description: The half-built single-storey house nearest the camera: its front wall of conventional brickwork (bricks laid flat, solid) raised to about the chest of a standing man, a door opening in the middle, two bamboo scaffold poles leaning at its left corner.
The top course of the near house's front wall: flat bricks with fresh grey mortar along them, an iron mortar pan resting on the wall top at the mason's right.
A waist-high stack of red burnt clay bricks on the sand about six metres along the street from the near house, broken brick bats at its foot.
A stack of plain, unprinted grey cement bags on a wooden pallet beside the brick stack, on the street side, one bag torn open with spilt cement dust.
The new sandy street from the stacks past the near house to the far houses, footprints and wheelbarrow tracks in the sand.
Three more half-built brick houses along the street beyond the near house, their walls at different heights, under neem and coconut trees.

shot.camera_reason: A slightly high wide view shows many houses rising at once, observational like the footage; the drift reveals the street going on.

scene.light: Warm late-morning sun from the upper left, hard, lighting the brick face, with soft shade under the neem trees; natural, muted, true-to-life colour.

landmarks.description: The unplastered three-storey front in rat-trap bond: red-orange bricks on edge with headers, grey joints, windows on all three floors, balconies on the upper floors with potted plants and washing.
The flat roof terrace above the third floor with a low parapet and a black water tank.
A low brick compound wall with an iron gate in front of the building, a two-wheeler parked just inside.
Neem trees at both sides of the street, framing the building.

shot.appearance: No departure from the shared appearance.
shot.camera: Still photograph, 35 mm equivalent, eye level about 1.6 m from the far side of the street, verticals straight; slow 5 percent push-in.
shot.camera_reason: An honest eye-level view from the street shows the three floors whole; the slow push draws the viewer toward the brickwork that carries them.
claims: Buildings up to three storeys can be safely built with rat-trap bond when constructed properly.
shot.evidence: The result in a scene: a finished, lived-in three-storey building whose exposed face shows rat-trap bond.
shot.focus: Deep focus across the whole building.
shot.framing: Wide from across the street, the whole building centred with its roof terrace and the front gate in frame, neem trees at both edges, a little sky above.
shot.information_progression: 1) Opens on the whole building, roof terrace to front gate. 2) The slow push-in narrows toward the brick face of the middle floor. 3) The building remains unchanged throughout.
shot.message: Built properly, rat-trap bond buildings can rise to three storeys.
shot.narration: When constructed properly, buildings up to three storeys can be safely built using this technology.
shot.purpose: Photographic AI still of a finished, lived-in three-storey building of exposed rat-trap bond brickwork in a tree-lined Tamil Nadu street, seen whole from across the street, with a slow push-in toward its brick face.
shot.review_notes: Check the candidate shows exactly three floors above ground (the roof terrace with its parapet and tank must not read as a fourth floor), the face in rat-trap bond with bricks on edge, no plaster, and no signboard or lettering.
shot.size_reason: All three storeys must be in view, roof to ground.
